Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

matrixprofiler 0.1.12

  • Native Multivariate STOMP (mstomp): Added native high-performance C++ engine (mstomp_rcpp) with multi-threading via RcppThread, properly sorting must/exclusion dimensions, and fixing historical edge cases where must dimensions could be omitted from accumulated distances. Delivers ~197x speedup over legacy pure R execution.
  • Missing Value Handling in Rolling Window Functions (na_strategy & na.rm): Implemented complete missing/non-finite value support across mov_mean(), mov_sum(), mov_var(), mov_std(), mov_min(), mov_max(), movmean_std(), and muinvn() with explicit na_strategy = c("window_na", "remove", "error") and standard na.rm argument compatibility. Default "window_na" returns NA_real_ strictly for windows intersecting non-finite values without corrupting adjacent valid windows or stopping execution.
  • Multithreaded MASS Variants (mass): Extended multi-threading via RcppThread to all MASS variants (v2, weighted, non_normalized, absolute) in mass() and C++ backend (mass2_rcpp, mass_weighted_rcpp, mass_absolute_rcpp), matching mass3_rcpp_parallel with identical numerical output.
  • Native MPdist Engine: Added native high-performance C++ implementation of MPdist (mpdist_vect_rcpp and mpdist_simple_rcpp) with multi-threaded parallel execution via RcppThread.
  • Zero Allocation & O(N) Sliding Min: Implemented linear-time monotonic deque for sliding window minimum and O(K)O(K) selection with std::nth_element, replacing expensive R matrix and data frame allocations and providing massive speedups (over 10x-100x).
  • Exported mpdist() API: Exported mpdist(ref_data, query_data, window_size, type = c("simple", "vector"), thr = 0.05, n_workers = 1) in R with dedicated unit test suite.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9013

  • CUDA RFCP Optimization: Replaced CUB Segmented Radix Sort with a parallel warp/block-level iterative top-KK reduction with exclusion zone support in inst/cuda/rfcp_gpu_poc.cu.
  • Zero In-Loop PCIe Synchronization: Removed all synchronous host-device transfers and pipeline flushes from the query loop, keeping query progression entirely asynchronous on the GPU.
  • Efficient Plato Retrieval: Eliminated repeated transfers of full distance vectors during record updates; distance profiles are now computed once post-loop for the winning Plato query.
  • Massive Speedup & Scalability: Drastically cuts per-query latency by up to ~100x and reduces device memory consumption from gigabytes down to tens of megabytes, preventing out-of-memory bottlenecks on multi-million sample series.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9012

  • Added query chunking and tiled execution support to rfcp_top_k() via query_block_size, dividing long query streams into bounded blocks while preserving exact numeric equivalence to monolithic execution.
  • Added progress_callback reporting structured events ("round_start", "block_done", "round_done") with execution timings and local block/Plato metrics.
  • Added serializable state checkpointing and resumption via checkpoint_callback and resume_state, supporting idempotent recovery from both intra-round (query block) and inter-round (Plato) interruptions.
  • Added unit test coverage for chunked invariance, mid-round and inter-round state resumption, callback events, and input/signature compatibility validation.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9011

  • Added adaptive_max_freq support to rfcp_top_k(), dynamically rescaling subsequent frequencies based on observed Plato support (count of positive self-join neighbors with distance below 2⋅window_size\sqrt{2 \cdot \text{window\_size}}) with configurable min_freq floor.
  • Added unit test coverage for adaptive frequency descent across dominant and secondary synthetic pulse morphologies.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9010

  • Added rfcp_top_k(), an iterative Top-K Plato discovery function for Relative Frequency Contrast Profiles (RFCP) that uncovers multiple distinct contrasting patterns between a positive and negative time series.
  • Implemented iterative morphology suppression by concatenating each discovered Plato and its accepted positive self-join neighbors into the negative series, incorporating an exclusion zone around each occurrence ([start - exclusion_radius, start + window_size - 1 + exclusion_radius]) and fusing overlapping intervals with NA barriers to prevent boundary artifacts.
  • Added support for dynamic max_freq specification across Plato iterations via vectors (e.g. max_freq = c(10, 3)).
  • Added unit tests for input validation, multi-morphology discovery, frequency scaling, early stopping thresholds, and S3 print methods.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9009

  • Added an optional CUDA backend for exact RFCP (Relative Frequency Contrast Profile) computations through rfcp(..., backend = "cuda"), with full support for finite and NA-barrier series, query subsetting, and full-profile matrix extraction (return_profiles = TRUE).
  • Accelerated candidate sorting and greedy neighbor selection 100% on the GPU using cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort and a specialized CUDA exclusion kernel, eliminating PCIe bandwidth bottlenecks and delivering up to 55x speedup over CPU-sorting GPU baselines and over 12x speedup compared to single-threaded CPU execution.
  • Added GPU regression and numerical equivalence tests against the native CPU implementation, verifying exact Plato detection and machine-precision distance profiles (10−1410^{-14}) on real datasets.
  • Kept CUDA source in inst/cuda/ and linked conditionally via MATRIXPROFILER_ENABLE_CUDA, preserving standard CUDA-free CRAN compatibility.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9008

  • Added an optional CUDA backend for exact MPX self-joins and AB-joins through mpx(..., backend = "cuda"), including finite and NA-aware inputs.
  • Added GPU regression coverage against the parallel CPU implementations for profiles, indices, validity masks, and CUDA-free builds.
  • Kept CUDA source and its local build helper distributed in inst/cuda/ while preserving the default CUDA-free CRAN build.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9007

  • Optimized RFCP worker execution by reusing covariance, candidate, rank, and exclusion buffers across query blocks and carrying exclusion stamps between blocks.
  • Made RFCP query tiling worker-aware: the native kernel now starts the first tile at query_begin, derives the tile size from the query count and effective worker count, and reports query_rows_per_task, n_tasks, and effective_workers for diagnostics while preserving the public rfcp() API.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9006

  • Completed the native NA-aware RFCP implementation with deterministic AA/AB neighbor ranks, restartable query blocks, compact Plato output, and optional allocation-guarded full-profile matrices.
  • Added adaptive MASS-style FFT initialization for large RFCP blocks while retaining direct initialization for small inputs; the implementation advances subsequent rows with a STOMP-style covariance recurrence.
  • Reused worker-local covariance, candidate, rank, and exclusion buffers across RFCP blocks, carrying exclusion stamps between blocks to reduce allocation and reset overhead.
  • Added RFCP correctness, barrier, tie-breaking, serial/parallel, block-composition, near-constant, and performance regression coverage.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9005

  • Added rfcp(), an exact parallel NA-aware Relative Frequency Contrast Profile implementation with deterministic greedy non-overlapping neighbor ranks, fixed-frequency RMSC semantics, restartable positive-query blocks, and an allocation-guarded full-profile validation mode.

  • Added the fused native rfcp_na_segmented_native_rcpp_parallel() kernel, which shares rolling normalization across AA and AB computations, initializes large blocks with a MASS-style FFT convolution, advances subsequent distance profiles with a STOMP-style covariance recurrence, respects non-finite barriers and non-normalizable windows, and avoids materializing the pairwise distance matrix.

  • Added independently selectable native finite-block segmentation for NA-aware MPX self-joins and AB-joins through na_strategy = "segmented_native" in mpx(), while retaining the monolithic implementation as the default.

  • Added native diagonal-tile sampling for s_size < 1, with explicit partial results and adaptive tile subdivision based on the configured parallel thread count.

  • Added global-coordinate reduction of native segmented profiles and indices, including cross-segment AB comparisons and exclusion-zone handling for AA joins.

  • Optimized native segmented scheduling for highly unbalanced segment lengths, added cache-bounded rectangular blocks for exact AA joins, and allowed it to mask constant or otherwise non-normalizable windows without reverting to the monolithic NA-aware kernel.

  • Set the native exact-AA block default to 8,192 windows and documented MATRIXPROFILER_NATIVE_AA_BLOCK_SIZE for cache-tuning large parallel NA-aware self-joins without changing the public mpx() API.

  • Validated the native segmented implementation on the full fixture: exact AA and AB runs completed with partial = FALSE, identical validity masks, and substantial wall-time reductions compared with the previous native and monolithic NA-aware paths.

  • Added regression and stress coverage against the monolithic NA-aware MPX implementation and STAMP for non-finite barriers, one-window segments, distance, correlation, and sampled computations.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9003

  • Clarified the MPX s_size semantics: values below 1 retain randomized anytime sampling, while s_size = 1 processes all diagonals in monotone order and may yield a less representative partial result if interrupted.

  • Added a numerically guarded finite fast path for NA-aware MPX and MPXAB, preserving the stable normalization path for constant or large-offset windows.

  • Reused parallel AB/BA worker scratch buffers per executor thread and limited mutex merges to ranges touched by each task.

  • Avoided allocating and writing profile-index vectors in parallel self- and AB-joins when idxs = FALSE.

  • Added an opt-in AB/BA worker profiler with per-task counts for pairs, invalid blocks, scratch resets, merges, mutex wait, and observed threads.

  • Added a conservative native restart path that skips dense invalid blocks in parallel NA-aware AB/BA joins while preserving the original recurrence for sparse barriers.

  • Kept complete NA-aware AB/BA joins in monotone diagonal order to reduce parallel scratch resets and merges; sampled joins retain randomized work order.

  • Added reproducible fixture benchmarks and a persistent optimization workplan for NA-aware segmentation and parallel reductions.

matrixprofiler 0.1.11.9000

  • Fixed parallel STOMP silently returning incomplete profiles when a worker received fewer query windows than the window size.
  • Fixed SIGFPE crashes in parallel STOMP and MPX for computations with fewer than 100 query windows or diagonals.
  • Fixed unsafe R and Rcpp API calls from TBB workers, including MASS result allocation and progress reporting, which could cause stack imbalance and abort forked workers.
  • Fixed the public parallel STOMP AB-join call omitting the left_right_profile native argument.
  • Added left and right profile computation to parallel STOMP and corrected exclusion-zone handling.
  • Fixed parallel MPX ignoring s_size and added validation for values outside the [0, 1] interval.
  • Fixed parallel thread options not being restored when STOMP or MPX failed or was interrupted.
  • Added the serial mpx_na_rcpp() implementation, which excludes windows containing NA, NaN, or infinite samples while allowing later valid windows to recover, and optimized its quadratic kernel to avoid costly Rcpp proxy accesses.
  • Optimized NA-aware moving normalization with direct contiguous storage and a hybrid parallel implementation; parallel MPX and MPXAB use it automatically for sufficiently large window workloads.
  • Added mpx_na_rcpp_parallel() with the same missing-data semantics as the serial implementation and support for partial computations through s_size; its worker kernel uses direct contiguous storage without R API calls.
  • Added the bidirectional mpxab_na_rcpp() AB-join for independently masking non-finite windows in both input series, with direct storage access in its quadratic kernel.
  • Added mpxab_na_rcpp_parallel() with matching bidirectional masks and partial-computation behavior, using direct contiguous storage inside its workers.
  • Updated mpx() to route self-joins and AB-joins automatically to the serial or parallel missing-data implementation whenever either input contains NA, NaN, or infinite values.
  • Fixed serial STAMP modifying input vectors in place while sanitizing non-finite samples.
  • Fixed serial STAMP AB-joins using the data validity mask for query windows instead of maintaining separate masks.
  • Fixed parallel STAMP modifying input vectors, ignoring invalid query windows, ignoring s_size, and calling unsafe R APIs from worker threads.
  • Fixed STAMP failures on short inputs by removing the runtime MASS grain-size benchmark and validating native arguments before index arithmetic.
  • Fixed serial and parallel SCRIMP failures on non-finite and constant windows, including a parallel segmentation fault caused by zero-variance divisions and worker-thread R API calls.
  • Fixed parallel SCRIMP ignoring s_size; its diagonal computation now shares the validated NA-aware MPX recurrence while serial PRE-SCRIMP still seeds sampled distance profiles.
  • Fixed SCRIMP AB-joins skipping diagonals, omitting s_size in the R-to-C++ call, rejecting unequal input lengths, and failing to mask non-finite windows independently in both series.
  • Fixed STAMP and SCRIMP thread options not being restored when a parallel computation failed.
  • Added regression coverage for short parallel joins, small MPX/STOMP inputs, partial MPX computations, STOMP AB-joins, and left/right profiles.
  • Added STAMP and SCRIMP regression tests against MPX/MPXAB for serial, parallel, AB-join, non-finite, constant-window, and anytime cases.
  • Added randomized MPX missing-data stress tests against serial STAMP and an independent brute-force implementation.

matrixprofiler 0.1.0

  • Initial implementation of this package.
  • This package will keep all core functions that will allow you to use the Matrix Profile concept as a toolkit.
  • It will be the main dependency of the already available package tsmp.
